temperature_scaling_expression.quote: double leakage_current = leakage_current_char_tmp * std::pow(10.0, (temp - char_temp) / temp_swing);
temperature_scaling_expression.meaning: leakage scales by 10^((Temperature - CharacterizedTemperature) / SubthresholdTempSwing) -- a decade of extra leakage for every SubthresholdTempSwing kelvin above CharacterizedTemperature.

dibl_vdd_scaling_expression.citation: tech/TechModel.cc:266 (final leakage_current_factor), computed inside calculateLeakageCurrentFactor using dibl_swing_ = subthreshold_swing / dibl (TechModel.cc:107,142)
dibl_vdd_scaling_expression.quote: double leakage_current_factor = vgs/s1 + (vds - vdd_)/s2;   // s2 == dibl_swing_
dibl_vdd_scaling_expression.single_transistor_note: For num_stacks_==1 (every plain BUF/INV/DFFQ leakage query in this codebase), the early-exit at TechModel.cc:204-207 sets the internal node voltage v[1]=vdd_ directly, so vds==vdd_ exactly and the DIBL term (vds-vdd_)/s2 is identically 0 -- DIBL only has a nonzero effect for stacked (NAND2/NOR2, num_stacks>=2) leakage queries.

min_off_current_application.classification: FLOOR, not a ceiling and not additive -- MinOffCurrent only raises the characterized-temperature current if width*OffCurrent*10^leakage_current_factor would otherwise fall below it; it never caps or adds to a larger value.

part4_compute_chain_stages_fix.rule_implemented: Stage count (whether from the auto ceil(log(count)/log(taper)) formula, or from an explicit *Stages override) is capped at a new computeAchievableStages(final_load_, taper_, cache_, sizes_) bound: the number of stages produced by simulating sizeBufChain()'s own backward walk (target /= taper each step, pick the largest available discrete size <= target) and stopping the count the instant a stage would land on the smallest available size (index 0) -- because every stage beyond that point can only ever land on index 0 again too (dividing an already-floored capacitance by taper again clears nothing bigger), which is exactly the ratio-1.0 padding condition being eliminated. The cap is applied at CONSTRUCT time (not just at sizing time) so the excess stage is never built into the timing graph at all, not built-then-detected. Verified safe to read the StdCellLib cache at construct time: DSENT.cc's constructTechModel() builds StdCellLib (which synchronously populates its cache in its own constructor, StdCellLib.cc:39) before any model, including DFFRAM, is ever construct()'d (DSENT.cc:309 precedes :330's buildModel() call).
part4_compute_chain_stages_fix.why: The discrete AvailableSizes list (7 entries: [1,2,4,6,8,12,16] for 7FinFET.txt) can only support a limited number of DISTINCT size steps between a chain's starting load and its floor. The old formula assumed a continuous size range and could request more stages than that -- every excess stage got clamped to the smallest available size by sizeBufChain(), producing a chain with one or more adjacent stages at IDENTICAL (minimum) size: a drive-strength ratio of exactly 1.0 between them, i.e. a stage that adds intrinsic gate delay with zero sizing/taper benefit whatsoever.

assertion_added.quote: ASSERT(!((chosen_idx == 0) && (prev_chosen_idx == 0)), "[Error] sizeBufChain -> chain contains a ratio-1.0 padding stage (two adjacent stages both clamped to the minimum available size). computeChainStages() should have capped the stage count before this point -- its achievable-stage bound is out of sync with this function.");

4_32.winner: BOTH CHAINS DISABLED beats both grids' stages=1 optimum

direct_connect_boundary_IMPORTANT_FINDIN.crossover_point: Between N=8 and N=16: at N=4 and N=8, disabling the buffer entirely (0 stages) beats the best buffered (stages=1) option found in the swept grid; from N=16 upward, buffered stages=1 wins and the margin grows sharply with N (e.g. at N=64, direct=1.907e-10s vs buffered=7.781e-11s -- buffered is 2.45x faster).

per_n_search.grid: stages in {1..6} x taper in {1.0,1.2,1.4,1.5,2,2.5,3,4,6}, N in {4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512}, B=32, EnableStages/EnableTaper only (RowClockStages/RowClockTaper held at shipped default 0/4 -- RowClock's own optimum doesn't move with N since B is fixed at 32 throughout this sweep)
per_n_search.fit_interpretation: delay = 1.0534e-11 * log2(N) + 2.6607e-11, R^2=0.8047 -- a log-linear relationship holds reasonably well (R^2=0.80) but is NOT a tight fit, because the selected taper itself changes discontinuously across the sweep (see regime change below), which the single global linear fit does not capture.

does_stages_1_still_win_everywhere.answer: NO -- it does not win everywhere, and this is a genuine finding, not an artifact. Restricting to the swept EnableStages{1..6}/RowClockStages{1..6} grids (never testing the '0 stages / direct-connect' option), stages=1 does win at all 4 canonical points and all 8 per-N points, reproducing the previous (padding-bug-era) task's headline claim -- but that claim was only ever comparing 1-6 stages against each other, never against 0. When the direct-connect boundary is included (as it should be, since EnableTaper<=0/RowClockTaper<=0 are valid, already-supported settings), stages=1 LOSES to 0 stages at the two smallest points tested (N=4 and N=8, B=32) and wins from N=16 upward. Report this plainly: the original 'stages=1 wins everywhere' claim is TRUE only within the 1-6 stage range, and FALSE once the 0-stage option is included at small N/small fanout.

does_n64_regime_boundary_survive.answer: YES, in a refined form. Within the 'stages=1 wins' regime (N>=16), the SELECTED TAPER shows a clear discontinuity at N=64: N=16 and N=32 prefer taper=6 (the upper edge of the swept range, confirmed a true local optimum by the taper-extension probe up to 24), while N=64, 128, 256, and 512 all prefer taper=1.0 (the lower edge -- effectively 'use the single largest available buffer that still fits under the target', since with only 1 stage a smaller taper divisor keeps the sizing target closer to the real final load). This taper regime boundary at N=64 is present in the corrected (both-fixes) model just as it was described for the (voided) padding-bug-era sweep -- it survives, though its underlying MEANING has changed (it is now a real taper-selection transition, not an artifact of stage-count padding, since padding is structurally impossible under the Part 4 fix).
